title: Model & Dependency Supply-Chain Security
interviewAnswer: Model artifacts, packages, containers and datasets are executable/trusted inputs to an AI system. I pin and scan dependencies, verify model provenance/checksums, avoid unsafe deserialization, use trusted registries and keep an SBOM where appropriate.
why: Loading an unknown checkpoint can be equivalent to running unknown code, and compromised dependencies can bypass every model-level safety control.
intuition: Treat models like software binaries, not passive data files.
deepDive: Pickle-based formats may execute code on load. Safer tensor formats, signatures/checksums, reproducible builds and image scanning reduce risk. Dataset poisoning is another supply-chain threat.
workedExample: Downloading a community `.pt` checkpoint and calling `torch.load` can execute malicious pickle payloads; prefer trusted sources and safer formats when possible.
commonMistakes: Assuming a model file cannot execute code.
Using floating dependency versions in production images.
followUps: How would you verify a model artifact?
production: CI/CD should scan dependencies/images, sign artifacts, restrict registry write access and keep provenance from training run to deployment.
